sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Kassel has just widened paid parking a long way. On 29 September 2025 the city parliament approved a large expansion of the fee zone, with the CDU, FDP and Greens in favour and AfD, SPD and the Left against [0]. From 1 May 2026, 368 new meters are being added to about 300 existing ones, and the fee area more than doubles by July 2026, introduced district by district. Non-residents pay €1 an hour or €6 a day [2]. The expanded zone covers Bad Wilhelmshöhe, Nord-Holland, Rothenditmold, Südstadt, Unterneustadt, Vorderer Westen, Wehlheiden and Wesertor [3]. The resident permit rose to a flat €110 a year, from a maximum of €30, and the city expected about €3 million of extra revenue a year [0][1]. Until then, resident fees of €21 to €30 had not changed in ten years [5].

Fee policy has swung before. An Amt 66 presentation of 2016 said the 2014 fee change had raised parking fees by about 60% and had displaced long-term parkers into the multi-storey car parks [7], and in 2018 the fee hours in zone II were cut from 9–20 to 9–18 [6]. Electric vehicles with a parking disc pay no fee on paid short-stay bays until the end of 2026 [8]. For the street layout, the city is updating its transport plan [10], and in March 2025 it turned one lane of Untere Königsstraße into a one-year dining trial [11]. A 2023 future concept for the centre recommends making the car parks more attractive as entry points while promoting non-motorised transport [24].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The biggest change to supply was a loss. The Garde du Corps garage near the Rathaus, opened in 1973, closed in early October 2024 because of significant cracks. Experts judged refurbishment uneconomic, and it must be demolished. The source gives 380 and 360 spaces in different places, and the city did not say whether new parking would be built [15]. Kassel's charging network had 479 charging points at 107 sites in June 2025, with more in planning [9].

Tourism drives the pressure at the edge. Parking around Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe is often full on weekends and during the water shows, and the transit company adds tram and bus services on event days [22]. documenta 16 is due to run from 12 June to 19 September 2027 [23]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres, on park-and-ride or on garage tariff changes.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Kassel data cover seven car parks with 2,798 spaces, four within 500 m of Friedrichsplatz (1,978 spaces) and three more than 2 km away: the Herkules visitor centre, Schloss Wilhelmshöhe and the Atrium at Wilhelmshöhe station. The Friedrichsplatz underground car park is run by the city's Parkhausgesellschaft [16], the Kurfürsten Galerie by Apcoa [18] and the Rathaus car park by the City of Kassel, which says one entrance is closed and opening hours are limited [20]. A parking directory lists Friedrichsplatz at €2.00 an hour and €20 a day, and the Kurfürsten Galerie at €1.70 an hour and €15 a day; both pages are undated [17][18]. We have no price data of our own for Kassel.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 24% on weekdays and 24% at weekends. The fullest is the Rathaus car park (61% on weekdays and 69% at weekends, 228 spaces), whose limited hours make that figure hard to compare. Atrium and Galeria follow at 32%, and Herkules at 26%. The two largest car parks are the emptiest in the centre: the 560-space Kurfürsten Galerie is 20% full and the 980-space Friedrichsplatz 18%. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Kassel.
